title: Odd–Even Advantage Curves for Multiple Encryption
summary: A slight advantage for the adversary in the odd-round case was observed when r equals one, but whether it persists relative to the even-round case for all positive r remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: In the ideal cipher model, determine whether the adversary-advantage curve for $(2r-1)$-round multiple encryption is slightly more favorable to the adversary than the curve for $2r$-round multiple encryption, for general positive integer $r$, and prove the claim or provide a counterexample. This fine-grained comparison is unresolved because the available analysis cannot verify the conjectured separation; the analogous behavior was observed for $r=1$ by Aiello et al.

scope.domain: Fine-grained security of multiple encryption through adversary-advantage curves.
assumptions: The comparison is made in the ideal cipher model.
parameters: r: a general positive integer indexing the compared odd and even round counts
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove the conjectured fine-grained ordering of the odd- and even-round advantage curves for general positive r, or provide a counterexample.

citations.label: The Security of Multiple Encryption in the Ideal Cipher Model

progress.summary: The source conjectures that the odd-round curve is slightly more favorable to the adversary, citing analogous behavior when r equals one. Its analysis is not fine-grained enough to verify the separation.
citation_labels: Yuanxi Dai et al., The Security of Multiple Encryption in the Ideal Cipher Model
